Yes. 
these applications, under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.') for releasing .
them on bail, during the pendency of trial, in case FIR No. 47 of 2023, dated 20th July, 2023,
registered with Police Station Darlaghat, District Solan, H.P., under Sections 20 and 29 of of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (hereinafter referred to as 'NDPS Act') and Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC') rt 2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to the applicants, they are young men of 22 and 20 years, respectively, having no criminal antecedents; they are innocent and have falsely been implicated and arrested, in this case.
3. According to the applicants, the investigation, in the present case, is almost complete and no useful purpose would be served by keeping them in the judicial custody.
4. The applicants have earlier tried their luck by moving applications, before the learned Special Judge-II, Solan, District Solan, H.P.

entities.text: Special Judge-II, Solan, District Solan, H.P.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, their bail applications have been dismissed vide order dated 14.08.2023.

5. Lastly, it has been asserted that the applicants are in judicial custody and no useful purpose would be served by keeping them in the judicial custody, that too, in the company of the hardened criminals.

Kunal vs State Of H.P on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45519177/
2 .

6. Apart from this, number of undertakings have also been given on behalf of the applicants, for which, the applicants are ready to abide by, in case, released on bail, of during the pendency of the trial.

7. On the basis of above facts, Mr. Anirudh Sharma, learned counsel appearing for the applicants,
has prayed that rt during the pendency of the trial, the applicants may kindly be released on bail.

8. When put to notice, the police has filed the status report disclosing therein that on 20-07-2023,
when, SHO Darlaghat along-with other police personnel, was on patrolling duty and traffic checking and reached at place Kararaghat, then, at about 4:15 A.M, a secret information was received that Manish Kumar (applicant) and Kunal (applicant) are coming towards Gayana from Sunni side, in Maruti 800 car bearing No. HP28A-7001 along-with Charas in their vehicle and if vehicle is checked, then, huge quantity of Charas could be recovered.
8.1.
Upon receiving this tip off, information under Section 42(2) of the Act was prepared and sent to Supervisory Officer through HHG Baldev.

Thereafter, independent witness i.e. Karam Chand,
Pradhan, GP Gayana was called to the .
spot.
At place near Gayana bifurcation, picketing was done, where, at about 5.30 A.M one Maruti 800 car
bearing
registration No. HP28A-7001
, being driven by its driver, of reached there from Sunni-Mangu side, which was signaled to stop.
The driver of the said car, on seeing police party, got perplexed.
In the presence of independent witnesses, their rt whereabouts were inquired.
The person on wheel had disclosed his name as Manish Kumar (applicant) whereas, the person sitting by the side of driver seat, disclosed his name as Kunal (applicant).
The raiding party gave their personal search to the accused persons.
Thereafter, the car of the accused persons was checked and on checking, near gear lever, one blue coloured carry bag, concealed under blue coloured mat was found.

The carry bag was searched, in the presence of witnesses, which was found containing black coloured substance in the form of balls (small and big) in transparent plastic packets.
8.2.
The recovered black coloured substance, on checking, was found to be Charas.
On weighing the contraband with digital machine, it was found to be 518 Grams.
The recovered Charas was put in the same manner in the same carry bag and sealed with seal impression 'A'.

NCB . 
Form in triplicate was filled, memos were prepared, photographs were clicked and police completed all other codal formalities.
The vehicle, along-with its key, was taken into possession vide separate memo.
The said act of accused came within the purview of Sections 20 and 29 of NDPS Act, rt therefore, rukka was prepared and sent to police station for registration of FIR.
After recording the statements of witnesses, accused persons were arrested.
The proceedings under Section 52-A of the Act were conducted.
Case property along-with vehicle, NCB form was deposited with MHC of the police station.
Special report was prepared and sent to Supervisory Officer.

Kunal vs State Of H.P on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45519177/
3 8.4.
Thereafter the case property was sent to SFSL, Junga and FSL report is still awaited.
Accused Manish (applicant) disclosed that he used to do work of Tyre Puncture and is addicted of consuming Charas, and in need of money, he used to sell the contraband.
Accused Kunal (applicant) also disclosed that he is driver by profession and both are friends, who are addicted of consuming Charas

Accused persons disclosed that on 18-07-2023, both of them purchased 518 Grams Charas at place Anni for a sum of .
90,000/- from an unknown person.

8.5. During investigation, it was found that vehicle bearing No. HP- 28A-7001 was registered in the name of one of Het Ram and accused Manish has prepared fake number plate of his vehicle and is not disclosing about exact number of his vehicle, nor he is having any documents regarding his rt vehicle.

8.6. Further, it is the case of the police that the requisite correspondences have been made to get the details about the movable and immovable property of the applicants and the report is still awaited.
Although, contraband has been sent to SFSL, Junga, however, the report of the same is still awaited.
8.7. Lastly, it has been submitted that investigation is going on, as such, a prayer has been made to dismiss the bail applications.

9. Heard.
10.
The contraband, allegedly recovered from the possession of the applicants, does not fall within the definition of 'commercial quantity'.
The same falls within the definition of 'intermediate quantity'.

Since the contraband, so recovered, does not fall within the commercial quantity, as .
such, rigors of Section 37 of the NDPS Act are not applicable, in the present case.

11. Once, it has been held that the rigors of Section of 37 of the NDPS Act are not applicable, then,
the presumption of innocence is still available to the accused.
12. No other criminal history of the bail applicants rt has been mentioned in the status report nor the same has been argued by learned Deputy Advocate General during the course of arguments.
Meaning thereby, the presumption of innocence is still available to the applicants.
13. The applicants are residents of District Solan and as such, it cannot be apprehended that they will not be available during the course of trial.

Considering the age of the applicants, they are entitled for the benefit of bail, keeping in view the fact that, keeping them in the company of hardened criminals, at this tender age, would adversely affect their future.

14. The applicants are in judicial custody and this fact demonstrates that their custodial interrogation is not required by the police, as the chances of commencement and conclusion of trial in near future are not so bright.
Moreover, the bail applications cannot be rejected as a matter of .

Kunal vs State Of H.P on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45519177/
4
punishment as pre-trial punishment is prohibited under the law.
15. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the of view that the bail applications are liable to be allowed and are accordingly allowed.

16. The applicants are ordered to be released on bail rt in case FIR No. 47 of 2023, dated 20th July,
2023, registered with Police Station Darlaghat, District Solan, H.P., under Sections 20 and 29 of NDPS Act and Section 420 IPC, on their furnishing personal bail bond, in the sum of 50,000/-
each, with one surety each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Solan/Judicial Magistrate First Class, Arki.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Solan/Judicial Magistrate First Class, Arki
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall of not be taken as an expression of opinion, on the merits of the case, as these observations, are confined, only, to the disposal rt of the present bail applications.
18. It is made clear that the respondent-State is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions, is found to be violated by the applicants.

19. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of Jail,
Solan through e- mail, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the e-prison software.

20. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of Jail, Solan is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary, DLSA, Solan.

The Superintendent of Jail, Solan is further directed that if the applicants fail to furnish the bail bonds,
as per the order passed by this Court, within a period of one month from today, then, the said fact be submitted to this Court.
